Geologic Hazards
The Project Area lies well outside the intermountain seismic belt. Several areas in eastern Montana have been identified as earthquake centers. According to Coffman and VonHake (1973), no historic earthquakes have been recorded within 100 miles of Tracts II and III that have had an intensity greater than VI. Based on the seismic history of southeastern Montana, it is unlikely any major destruction will occur in the Project Area as a result of regional earthquakes.
Soils
Soils in the area have weathered from a variety of sandstone, siltstone and shale strata which have been exposed by erosion of the Fort
Union Formation. Soil textures range from sandy loam to clay loam.

Much of the weathered material has been transported into drainages and
deposited to form deep, fertile alluvial soils used primarily for alfalfa
hay and farming of small grain. Residual soils on uplands and ridges
range from very shallow to moderately deep, and the more favorable sites
are suitable for farming.
Maps II-1 and II-2 are soil maps of Tract II and Tract III, respectively. The Tract II map was extracted from the Big Horn County Soil Survey, which is currently being published by the Soil Conservation Service (SCS). The SCS used the "letter system" of mapping unit classification. Tract III was mapped for Westmoreland Resources by James C. Meshnick (SCS, Retired) who utilized the "numerical-letter system".
